How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to generate a RESTful API request for the **“get information of device connector versions”** API (version 6.3.1) in Cisco Nexus Dashboard. I’ll also show you how to call the same endpoint programmatically using the `requests_get` function you have available. --- ## 1. Using the Cisco Nexus Dashboard UI | Step | What to do | Why it matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Log in** | Open your browser → `https:///login` → Enter your credentials. | You need an authenticated session to access the API Explorer. | | **2. Go to the API Explorer** | From the left‑hand navigation pane, click **“Developer” → “API Explorer”**. | The API Explorer is the built‑in tool that lets you browse, test, and generate code snippets for all available APIs. | | **3. Select the API** | In the API Explorer search bar, type **“device connector versions”** or the exact API name “get information of device connector versions”. | This filters the list to the API you’re interested in. | | **4. Choose the API version** | At the top of the API details page, there’s a drop‑down labeled **“API Version”**. Pick **6.3.1**. | Different API versions may have different parameters or response schemas. | | **5. Fill in required parameters** | The API page lists all required and optional parameters. For this API you’ll typically need:
• `connectorId` (string) – the ID of the connector you want info for.
• `includeDetails` (boolean, optional) – whether to include detailed version info. | Parameters are passed either as query strings or in the request body, depending on the API design. | | **6. Click “Generate Request”** | After filling in the parameters, click the **“Generate Request”** button. | The tool will build the full HTTP request (method, URL, headers, body). | | **7. Review the generated request** | A panel opens showing:
• **Method** (GET, POST, etc.)
• **URL** (including query parameters)
• **Headers** (Authorization, Content‑Type, etc.)
• **Body** (if applicable) | Verify that the URL matches your environment and that the Authorization header contains a valid bearer token. | | **8. Copy the code snippet** | Below the request preview, there’s a “Copy Code” button. Click it to copy the snippet in your preferred language (Python, JavaScript, cURL, etc.). | You can paste this into your IDE or terminal to execute the request directly. | ### Example of what you’ll see ``` GET https://api.nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v6.3.1/device-connectors/12345/versions?includeDetails=true Headers: Authorization: Bearer Accept: application/json ``` --- ## 2. Programmatic Call Using the `requests_get` Function If you prefer to call the API from code (e.g., in a script or a notebook), you can use the `requests_get` function you have. Here’s how: ```python from functions import requests_get # Base URL for the Nexus Dashboard API (replace with your actual host) BASE_URL = "https://api.nexus-dashboard.example.com" # Endpoint path for the specific API (you can find this in the API Explorer) ENDPOINT = "/api/v6.3.1/device-connectors/{connectorId}/versions" # Replace {connectorId} with the actual ID you want to query connector_id = "12345" endpoint = ENDPOINT.format(connectorId=connector_id) # Full URL url = f"{BASE_URL}{endpoint}" # Optional query parameters params = { "includeDetails": "true" # or False / omitted if not needed } # Call the function response = requests_get(url=url, params=params) # Inspect the result print(response) ``` **What the function does internally** - Builds the full URL with query parameters. - Adds the necessary headers (Authorization, Accept, etc.) automatically if configured in your environment. - Performs an HTTP GET request. - Returns the parsed JSON response (or raw text if parsing fails). --- ## 3. Things to Keep in Mind | Topic | Tips | |-------|------| | **Authentication** | Most Nexus Dashboard APIs require a bearer token. Make sure you have a valid token and that the `requests_get` function is configured to inject it into the `Authorization` header. | | **Rate limits** | Check the API documentation for any rate‑limit headers (`X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`). | | **Error handling** | The API Explorer shows sample error responses. In your code, handle non‑200 status codes gracefully (e.g., retry logic, logging). | | **Environment variables** | Store sensitive data (host, token) in environment variables or a secrets manager rather than hard‑coding them. | | **Testing** | Use the “Test” button in the API Explorer to validate your parameters before generating code. | --- ## 4. Quick Reference: Generated cURL Snippet If you prefer to run the request from the command line, the API Explorer can generate a cURL command: ```bash curl -X GET "https://api.nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v6.3.1/device-connectors/12345/versions?includeDetails=true" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` Just replace `` with a real token and `12345` with the connector ID you’re querying. --- ### Recap 1. **Navigate** to the API Explorer in Nexus Dashboard. 2. **Select** the “get information of device connector versions” API and choose version 6.3.1. 3. **Fill in** the required parameters and click **Generate Request**. 4. **Copy** the generated code snippet or use the `requests_get` function to call the endpoint programmatically.
